subproblem.title: Continuity of the inverse of a Simon local representation on W ∩ M (Simon 2.4.2)
subproblem.statement: Let n, N ∈ ℕ, r ∈ ℕ∞, M ⊆ ℝᴺ, V ⊆ ℝⁿ, W ⊆ ℝᴺ and ψ : ℝⁿ → ℝᴺ satisfy IsSimonLocalRepresentation r M V W ψ: V and W are open, ψ is C^r on V, ψ is injective on V, ψ(V) = W ∩ M, V ∩ ψ⁻¹(K) is compact for every compact K ⊆ W, and Dψ(x) is injective for every x ∈ V. Let g := Function.invFunOn ψ V : ℝᴺ → ℝⁿ. Here g(y) is a point of V mapped to y by ψ whenever such a point exists, and a fixed arbitrary point of ℝⁿ otherwise. Then g is continuous on W ∩ M in the relative topology, that is, ContinuousOn g (W ∩ M).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n N : ℕ) (r : ℕ∞) (M : Set (Rn N)) (V : Set (Rn n)) (W : Set (Rn N)) (ψ : Rn n → Rn N), Chapter02.IsSimonLocalRepresentation r M V W ψ → ContinuousOn (Function.invFunOn ψ V) (W ∩ M)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 1 of the parent-supplied proof of simon_submanifold_tangent_basics, written out for the inverse map g = Function.invFunOn ψ V. This is Simon, Introduction to GMT, Ch. 2, 4.2, p. 55, where the printed text only says that the definition ensures the local representation is a homeomorphism of V onto M ∩ W.

Hypotheses used: V and W are open; ψ is C^r on V for some r ∈ ℕ∞; ψ is injective on V; ψ(V) = W ∩ M; and V ∩ ψ⁻¹(Q) is compact for every compact Q ⊆ W. Injectivity of Dψ is not needed.

Proof.
1. ψ is continuous on V. A C^r map on V (any r ≥ 0) is continuous on V. Since V is open, ψ is continuous at every point of V.
2. g inverts ψ on W ∩ M. Let y ∈ W ∩ M. Since ψ(V) = W ∩ M, some a ∈ V has ψ(a) = y, so by the definition of invFunOn, g(y) ∈ V and ψ(g(y)) = y. Since ψ is injective on V, g(y) is the unique point of V mapped to y. In particular g(ψ(x)) = x for every x ∈ V.
3. Reduction to sequences. ℝⁿ and ℝᴺ are metric spaces, hence first countable. So g is continuous within W ∩ M at a point y ∈ W ∩ M as soon as g(y_j) → g(y) for every sequence (y_j) in W ∩ M with y_j → y. Fix y ∈ W ∩ M and such a sequence, and put x_j := g(y_j) and x := g(y). By step 2, x_j, x ∈ V, ψ(x_j) = y_j and ψ(x) = y.
4. A compact set containing all x_j. Q := {y_j : j ∈ ℕ} ∪ {y} is compact, being a convergent sequence together with its limit. Q ⊆ W, because every y_j and y lie in W ∩ M. By relative properness, K := V ∩ ψ⁻¹(Q) is compact. Each x_j lies in V with ψ(x_j) = y_j ∈ Q, so x_j ∈ K.
5. Subsequential limits. Let (x_{j_k}) be any subsequence. K is a compact subset of the metric space ℝⁿ, hence sequentially compact, so some further subsequence (x_{j_{k_l}}) converges to a point x′ ∈ K ⊆ V. By step 1, ψ is continuous at x′, so ψ(x_{j_{k_l}}) → ψ(x′). But ψ(x_{j_{k_l}}) = y_{j_{k_l}} → y. By uniqueness of limits ψ(x′) = y = ψ(x), and injectivity of ψ on V gives x′ = x.
6. Convergence. Suppose x_j does not converge to x. Then there are ε > 0 and a subsequence with |x_{j_k} − x| ≥ ε for all k. By step 5 this subsequence has a further subsequence converging to x, a contradiction. Hence g(y_j) = x_j → x = g(y).
7. Conclusion. By steps 3 and 6, g is continuous within W ∩ M at every point of W ∩ M, that is, ContinuousOn (Function.invFunOn ψ V) (W ∩ M).

Formal references:
- SimonGMT Chapter02.IsSimonLocalRepresentation.isProperMap_chartMap and isEmbedding_chartMap (Poincare/SimonGMT/Chapter02/SubmanifoldTopology.lean) prove the equivalent statement that the corestriction V → W of ψ is a closed topological embedding.
- Mathlib: Function.invFunOn_mem, Function.invFunOn_eq, Set.InjOn.leftInvOn_invFunOn, Filter.Tendsto.isCompact_insert_range, IsCompact.tendsto_subseq.
proof_key_steps: ψ is continuous at every point of the open set V (C^r implies C⁰). g = invFunOn ψ V returns the unique ψ-preimage in V of every y ∈ W ∩ M = ψ(V).
Reduce continuity on W ∩ M to sequences y_j → y in W ∩ M, since metric spaces are first countable.
Q = {y_j} ∪ {y} is compact and contained in W, so relative properness makes V ∩ ψ⁻¹(Q) a compact set containing every x_j = g(y_j).
Every subsequence of (x_j) has a further subsequence converging to some x′ ∈ V with ψ(x′) = y, so x′ = g(y) by injectivity. The sub-subsequence criterion then gives g(y_j) → g(y).
